### Electron Version

39.0.0

macOS

### Operating System Version

Tahoe 26.0.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

I have a Swift native add-on which calls ASAuthorization API (`ASAuthorizationController.performRequests()`) to create or request passkey authorization using macOS API. Expected behavior is that it would show authorization sheet proposing to authenticate using passkeys.

### Actual Behavior

I have a Swift native add-on which calls ASAuthorization API (`ASAuthorizationController.performRequests()`) to create or request passkey authorization using macOS API. The problem is, when the API is called, I get error:
```
The calling process does not have an application identifier. Make sure it is properly configured.
```
System logs tell something like:
```
Attempted to perform authorization from process without application identifier.
...
Could not perform authorization: ... AuthorizationError Code=1
ASAuthorizationController ... Code=1004 ... “told not to present authorization sheet”,
```
I have properly set up code signing in the app using Developer ID Certificate, even created Developer ID Application provision profile - electron-builder says code signing and notarization go ok. I've specified required entitlements and checked provision profile embedded in .app contains that entitlements. I tested on distribution build mode. 

Does anybody have any ideas on what could be wrong with the signing options of `electron-builder` or probably native add-on build settings to produce such error? Thanks for any help in advance.

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: [Docs] document that will-navigate can be triggered via (child? arbitrary?) frame
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Problem Description The documentation in https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-contents#event-will-navigate currently has: > initiator WebFrameMain | null (optional) - The frame which initiated the navigation, which can be a parent frame (e.g. via window.open with a frame's name), or null if the navigation was not initiated by a frame. This can also be null if the initiating frame was deleted before the event was emitted. There's one more case that could be documented here -- an unsandboxed iframe can also trigger navigation in the main frame via a link with something like `Click here`. ### Proposed Solution Include this scenario as one of the potential ways a frame could navigate. ### Alternatives Considered Simply document that the frame that initiates navigation, and the frame that is actually being navigated, might differ. ### Additional Information _No response_

### Electron Version

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubutu 25.04

### What arch are you using?

x86_64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

The codebase should use modern, non-deprecated string methods (`.substring()` or `.slice()`) instead of `.substr()`. This ensures:
- No deprecation warnings in development tools
- Better future compatibility with JavaScript engines
- Adherence to current ECMAScript standards
- Consistency with modern JavaScript best practices

### Actual Behavior

The codebase currently uses the deprecated `.substr()` method in 5 locations across different files. While this still works functionally, it triggers deprecation warnings in modern development environments and violates current JavaScript best practices. The method may be removed in future JavaScript versions, which could cause potential compatibility issues.

_No response_

nodes.title: Running Sharp's `.metadata()` hangs and crashes electron.
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.0.0 - 37.8.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Fedora 43 / Linux x1f 6.17.6-300.fc43.x86_64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed Oct 29 20:10:51 UTC 2025 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

The code when run in electron:
```javascript
require('sharp')('./image.png')
	.metadata()
        .then(
        	m => console.log('OK:', m),
        	e => console.log('ERR', e))
```

Should produce:
```
PRE
POST
OK: {
  format: 'png',
  width: 212,
  height: 48,
  space: 'srgb',
  channels: 4,
  depth: 'uchar',
  density: 72,
  isProgressive: false,
  isPalette: false,
  bitsPerSample: 8,
  hasProfile: false,
  hasAlpha: true,
  autoOrient: { width: 212, height: 48 }
}
TIMEOUT
```

This works as expected when: 
1. running code in electron repl:  
  ```shell
  npx electron -i
  ```
  then
  ```javascript
  require('./test')
  ```
3. running from node (see code in gist):  
  ```shell
  node ./test.js
  ```


### Actual Behavior

When running via:
```shell
npx electron .
```

The code _hangs_ on the `.metadata()` call and then is killed with SIGSEGV:
```
electron exited with signal SIGSEGV
```


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/flynx/ed7ffbc9697586fa36ed416251826157

### Additional Information

This issue can be reproduced on electron version from 37.0.0 and above, and [sharp](https://www.npmjs.com/package/sharp) versions 0.34.0 and above.

Can't seem to reproduce this error with other sharp API methods nor in any other context other than electron.

This seemed to work before the upgrade to Fedora43, but can't pinpoint what exactly changed that could affect this (glibc, kernell, ...?).

Possibly related to: #46323

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

能够正常触发鼠标移入事件

### Actual Behavior

条件一：在置顶electron窗口的下层窗口是chrome内核的窗口；条件二：electron窗口设置鼠标忽略{forwards:true}。 导致：会出现在触摸屏上点击该窗口 无法触发鼠标移入事件，两个条件任一不满足则不会有该问题。 例如 electron窗口下方是桌面 或是记事本时 能够正常触发鼠标移入事件。
THIS IS ENGLISH DESCRIPTION=>Condition 1: The window under the topmost Electron window uses the Chrome engine; Condition 2: The Electron window is set to ignore the mouse {forwards:true}. Result: On a touchscreen, clicking this window will not trigger the mouse enter event. If either of the two conditions is not met, this issue will not occur. For example, if the window beneath the Electron window is the desktop or Notepad, the mouse enter event can be triggered normally.

### Problem Description

`BrowserWindow.isSnapped()` was added for Windows: https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/46079.

Electron also detects window tiling changes on Linux but does not surface this state to consumers in JS.

### Proposed Solution

Electron could plumb Linux tiling state to the existing `isSnapped()` method, even though this state is called "tiling" on Linux.

### Alternatives Considered

A new Linux only `isTiled()` method would be more accurately named for Linux but probably not worth it.

### Proposed Solution

I already have a basic hello world application working on the android emulator. But the code needs cleanup, and there is a ton of work needed for feature parity. Before I invest more time into it, I wanted to hear from the maintainers. Are you supportive of the idea? Do you have any major concerns? Anything you'd like me to consider?

Looking forward to the discussion.

### Alternatives Considered

I know that alternatives to electron exist for android (e.g cordova). But I'm specifically interested in electron on android.

nodes.body:

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38.4.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windos 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

The existing native print dialog should be brought to the foreground and receive focus, allowing the user to interact with it.

### Actual Behavior

The print dialog remains in the background, out of view. The user cannot see the dialog appear on the screen, giving the impression that the print button is broken or unresponsive. A new dialog is not created (which is correct behavior for modal dialogs), but the existing one is not focused.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/mksreddy48-dev/f5bd2d017dbec360a917021017f67dac

### Additional Information

When a user triggers the native print dialog in an Electron application (using either window.print() in the renderer or mainWindow.webContents.print() in the main process), if the dialog is dismissed or moved to the background, triggering the print command again does not bring the existing dialog to the foreground. The dialog remains hidden behind the main Electron application window or other running applications.
This behavior prevents users from interacting with the print dialog a second time without manually searching for it in their OS taskbar/dock.

nodes.title: Electron freezes when trying to send a Notification without a notification daemon running
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 39.0.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version Arch Linux (all distros are affected) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version N/A ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior The notification should simply fail to send ### Actual Behavior The app freezes for 1 minute ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/Vendicated/6f8d74229835950e1aeb5f43b74e1f92 ### Additional Information The root issue seems to be that `notify-send hi` will fail and get stuck until it times out after 1 minute. So the suggested fix is to make sure that notify-send is called asynchronously instead of waiting for it to exit. This issue doesn't happen on Chromium. This issue was already reported in the past but got automatically closed due to the tested Electron version no longer being supported: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/21912 This is a widespread issue that affects every Electron app. See for example: - https://github.com/signalapp/Signal-Desktop/issues/2567 - https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Discord#Discord_freezes_after_getting_pinged_or_messaged - https://github.com/element-hq/element-web/issues/32396 Reproducing this is a bit inconsistent. For example I can't reproduce on Hyprland with no Notification daemon, but can reproduce on KDE Plasma with Notifications disabled. ## Reproduction Steps (KDE Plasma) 1. Install and run KDE Plasma 2. Right click the little Tray caret and click "Configure System Tray" 3. In "Entries", set "Notifications" to Disabled 4. Log out and back in 5. Run the attached Fiddle and click the Show Notification button 6. Observe that the App becomes unresponsive 7. Run `notify-send hi` in a terminal 8. Observe that it freezes until it times out
Reproduction Screenshots
